title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD, design spec, roadmap, pricing & release notes (Q2 2026)
author: Maya Patel
summary: Comprehensive product document combining the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design decisions, roadmap themes for Q2–Q4 2026, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Q2 2026 release of Unified Inference. This doc is intended for cross-functional stakeholders (product, engineering, sales, finance, and support) and serves as the source of truth for go-to-market and implementation plans.
overview:
Background: Redwood's Unified Inference product provides a single API and operational surface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The objective for the 2026 roadmap is to: 1) make production-grade inference easier to adopt for engineering teams, 2) reduce running costs through automated controls and recommendations, and 3) provide predictable enterprise-grade contracts for Dedicated and Private customers.

Scope of this document: - Product goals and success metrics - Functional & non-functional requirements (PRD) - Design highlights and system constraints - Roadmap by quarter and themes - Pricing and packaging proposals, migration guidance - Release notes for the Q2 2026 feature drop

Audience: Product, Engineering, Sales, Finance, Customer Success, Security.
product_goals_and_success_metrics:
Goals: - Lower unit inference cost for typical web-app workloads by 20% (via batching, caching, quantization recommendations) - Increase MRR from Dedicated commitments by 30% Y/Y through clearer packaging and upsell paths - Reduce time-to-onboard for Private deployments to < 4 weeks for qualified customers

Success metrics (KPIs): - Avg token cost per model family (baseline vs current) — target: -20% - % of requests benefiting from prefix/KV cache — target: > 35% - Dedicated conversion rate (free -> committed) — target: 12% per quarter - Private deployment time to first inference (days) — target: median 21 days - Customer satisfaction (NPS for onboarding) — target: +10 vs baseline
requirements:
Overview: Requirements below are prioritized into Must / Should / Nice-to-have. Each requirement includes acceptance criteria and owner.

Table: prioritized requirements
| id | requirement | priority | owner | acceptance criteria |
| R-001 | Per-route cost & latency controls (max_tokens_per_request, preferred_model_families, fallback_policy) | Must | Product/Runtime | API parameter exists; console UI; enforcement at routing layer; unit tests + e2e policy test |
| R-002 | Automated batching & cache suggestions (Optimize) surfaced in Console | Must | Product/Optimize | Console shows suggested batching window and cache TTL with projected cost delta; pilot on 10 customers |
| R-003 | Reserved capacity packaging (monthly/annual) with burst & rollover rules | Must | Finance/Product | Contract templates; billing integration; SLA page; integration tests with billing; two pilot customers signed |
| R-004 | Pricing engine that supports blended per-token + reservation pricing & per-route discounts | Must | Finance/Backend | Accurate invoice for test scenarios; pricing simulation tool; migration plan from legacy billing |
| R-005 | Private deployment installer & bootstrap automation (VPC + onprem variant) | Should | Eng Private Deployments | Automated scripts for VPC peering and KMS setup; documented runbook; successful internal dry-run |
| R-006 | Model quantization recommendation engine and compatibility matrix | Should | Applied ML | Report with recommended quantization per model and estimated perf/cost impact; compatibility page in model catalog |
| R-007 | Usage-based free tier and clear upgrade path in Console | Nice-to-have | Growth/Product | Console flows implemented; A/B test shows higher trial->paid conversion |

Non-functional requirements: - 99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated endpoints (measured monthly) - 95th percentile latency targets per route must be configurable and enforced by routing policies - Audit logging for billing-sensitive operations retained for 13 months
design_spec:
High-level design decisions: 1) Pricing & Billing: decouple meter collection from billing aggregation. Metering will emit per-request records (route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, quantization, hardware_tier). The billing pipeline aggregates at daily and contract-window levels.

2) Routing / Policy Enforcement: requests carry route metadata; smart-router evaluates policy (latency SLO, cost budget, region) and picks model variant. Fallbacks are explicit (e.g., 'downgrade-quantization', 'variant-shorter-context', 'region-fallback') and encoded as a chain.

3) Console UX: dedicated Pricing page with simulator (inputs: monthly active tokens, % host vs dedicated, committed hours). Also: Per-route cost graphs and actionable suggestions (enable batching, increase TTL).

4) Data & Metrics: add the following metering fields to the telemetry spec: model_variant_id, quantization_profile, batch_size, cache_hit (bool), billing_tag, customer_tier. Use the existing observability pipeline (Prometheus + ClickHouse for short-term; long-term aggregated storage in Redshift) to power dashboards.

Performance & scale constraints: - Billing pipeline must support 10M meter events/day at GA scale; design supports partitioning by customer_id and date - Router decision latency budget: < 1ms median, < 5ms p95 extra overhead

Security considerations: - Pricing simulation data includes PII-free usage samples only when explicit consent from customer - Private deployments must support customer-managed KMS for key rotation and audit hooks
roadmap_and_themes:
Q2 2026 (Now -> Jun 2026) — Stabilize pricing engine and launch reserved capacity SKU - Deliver billing engine MVP, contract templates, and two pilot Dedicated customers - Console: pricing simulator, per-route cost breakdowns, suggestions panel - Runtime: expose per-request metering fields and basic fallback policies

Q3 2026 (Jul -> Sep 2026) — Automations & Optimize integration - Auto-batching recommendation rollout (Optimize v2) - Quantization recommendation engine initial release and compatibility matrix - Improve cost SLO routing policies; enable region and tier-based fallbacks

Q4 2026 (Oct -> Dec 2026) — Enterprise polish and Private GA - Private deployment automation improvements; reduce setup time to target 14 days - Advanced reserved capacity features: rollover hours, multi-region pools - Billing GA, full reporting and revised pricing tiers for enterprise customers

Themes: "Reduce friction to commit", "Make unit economics visible and actionable", "Scale private deployments with repeatable automation"
pricing_and_packaging_notes:
High-level packaging proposal (internal draft): - Starter (self-serve): usage-based only; free tier 100k tokens / month; pay-as-you-go per 1M tokens $X (internal reference price: $3.50 per 1M input tokens, $7.00 per 1M output tokens) -- intended for dev/test and early PLG funnel. - Scale (mid-market): usage-based with volume discounts and Per-route controls; recommended for SMBs. Example: 5% discount at 5M tokens/month, 15% at 50M+/month. Access to Optimize recommendations. - Dedicated (enterprise): reserved capacity (monthly or annual) with guaranteed throughput and 99.9% SLA; includes burst policy, per-route quotas, and dedicated cost dashboard. Pricing: commit-based discounted rate (example effective token rate target 40-60% lower than Starter). - Private (enterprise+): license + deployment fee + annual support. Pricing and SOW based on region, compliance, and runbook integration.

Discount & billing rules (examples): - Bursts: customers can burst above commit up to 2x for up to 24 hours; overage billed at on-demand rate + 10% premium. - Rollover: monthly commit can roll over up to 10% of unused hours to next month (Enterprise only). - Migrations: legacy customers on previous plans will be migrated using an opt-in window with a 6-month transition period and pro-rated proration.

Key open questions for GTM and Finance: 1) What is the public per-token list price for Starter vs Scale? (Finance to finalize) 2) How to present per-route pricing in the Console without overwhelming customers? (UX to prototype) 3) What are the enterprise discount floors (sales policy)? (Sales & Finance to finalize)
release_notes:
Release: Unified Inference v2026.04 (released 2026-04-15) Highlights: - Billing engine MVP: per-request metering and daily aggregation enabled for all customers in staging; two Dedicated customers onboarded to pilot reserved capacity contracts. - Console: Pricing simulator (beta) and per-route cost breakdown dashboard (read-only for Starter; actionable suggestions for Scale/Dedicated). - Runtime: added request-level telemetry fields (model_variant_id, quantization_profile, cache_hit) and router support for simple fallback policies.

Migration notes & breaking changes: - Metering schema change: new required field billing_tag added to metering records. Customers with custom ingestion must update their ingestion adapters before 2026-05-01 or risk missing aggregated billing. - API compatibility: No changes to client-facing inference API in this release.

Known issues: - Pricing simulator underestimates impact of quantization for some model families (working with Applied ML). - Console suggestion panel shows duplicates for routes that have multiple billing tags (fix scheduled for 2026-04-28).
rollout_and_migration_plan:
Rollout approach: 1) Beta (Apr 15 -> May 15): internal + 5 pilot customers for Dedicated pricing and billing. Monitor invoicing accuracy and SLOs. 2) Early access (May 15 -> Jun 30): selected paying customers (Scale tier) get access to pricing simulator and suggestions. 3) GA (Jul 01): public launch for Starter/Scale; Dedicated features available via contract.

Migration steps for existing customers: 1. Communication: email + console banner detailing change and timeline (by Apr 20). 2. Technical: provide schema migration guide for metering_tag and example ingestion adapter. 3. Billing: offer opt-in pricing migration window (90 days). 4. Support: designate two CSMs as migration leads for pilot customers.

Monitoring & rollback criteria: - Stop GA if ten or more customers report invoice > 5% discrepancy versus expected or any Dedicated customer experiences > 2 SLO violations in a 7-day window. - Rollback path: revert billing aggregation to legacy pipeline (procedural runbook in eng-finance)
